Part 2. You will hear the warden of a nature trail talking to a group of people who are interested in hiking on the trail.
First you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14. Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.
Good morning. I'm Susan Meyer, trail warden for the McFadden Hiking and Nature Trail.
trail. Let me tell you a bit about the trail. The trail is 25 miles long, running roughly
east to west. To hike it, you may start at either end of the trail or in between. You
can hike the whole length of the trail or just a couple of miles because there are 20 entry
points along the trail, each connected to public roads by short paths.
For hikers coming from Johnson City, there's a shuttle bus to each of the two end points
every morning and evening.
And four of the entry points have a free car park with television camera surveillance.
At one-mile intervals along the trail, there are rest stations providing picnic areas, water,
toilets, and places where you can recharge your electronic devices.
In response to a poll of walkers last year, we've recently installed kiosks at each
rest station with clear, easy-to-follow maps and other trail information.
There are several distinct sections of trail.
The Red Rock Walk offers a superb opportunity to study a huge variety of vegetation along
along the way. There's lots to look at, though you can't see great distances. Birds are actually
hard to spot, but with a pair of binoculars and at certain times of day, you may see some
rare varieties. The Riverwalk comprises about five miles of trail winding along the bank
of the Malder River. Personally, I prefer this section of the trail in winter. The
river does freeze over and the snow can accumulate, but that doesn't always
discourage visitors. Sometimes though, if the weather conditions are really
unsuitable, we might have to close this walk to the public. But often it can
get crowded with hikers who've discovered the attraction of the area.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15-20.
Now listen and answer questions 15-20.
Now let me tell you about the Halfway Hostel, located approximately midway along the trail.
It has a range of facilities available to help make your walking experience memorable.
available. Let me give you some information about the various facilities available there.
Of course there are beds in dormitories for use at a very reasonable $7 per person, weekdays

There are two family rooms accommodating six people each with private bathrooms.
They're $35 per room and for them you will need to make arrangements ahead of time as they're very popular, especially at the weekends.
A popular facility that we've recently added is coin-operated washing machines for your clothes.
You can get awfully wet and dirty if you're walking the trail in bad weather,
and since we got these machines, you can put on clean gear when you set out in the morning.
The hostel serves two meals a day, breakfast at $4 and dinner at $8,
the same for adults and kids. There's always a vegetarian and a non-vegetarian option,
depending on your preferences.
We do ask you to give a hand with serving and cleaning up after meals.
We have plenty of showers and unlimited hot water available so you can have this luxury
at no charge and you can enjoy it as long as you like.
Now some people like to spend time on the trail on mountain bikes and maybe take a bit of
rest from all that walking and that's permitted as long as you observe basic safety rules.
The hostel is in the process of creating a bike rental scheme which should be up and running
next year.
So if you think that is the end of part 2, you now have 30 seconds to check your answers

Part 3. You will hear two business students called Janet and Michael discussing their research

21 to 26. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 26.

Hi, Michael. It's interesting. I've read how shampoo marketing has developed over the last
hundred years.

Right.

Part 4 You will hear a lecturer giving a talk on how
science may change in the future. First you have some time to look at questions 31 to 40.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 31 to 40.
In this final lecture of our course on the history of science, I would like to look to
the future and tell you about some predictions that have been made about scientific developments.
contents. The content for my talk is based on some research in which thirty scientific
leaders were invited to comment on the developments that they envisage as likely to come about
in their own discipline within fifty years. After summarizing some of their most interesting
contributions for you, I'll ask you to give me your opinions as to the likelihood of
these changes occurring within this time scale. You may also like to suggest some other likely
changes yourselves.
So first, let's start with computer science, as this is clearly an area where there are
bound to be dramatic developments, and even more significantly perhaps, these developments
are likely to impact on every other field of learning.
The invention of computers represents an enormous leap forward in the field of human endeavor.
It could indeed be considered as being as momentous a development as when our predecessors in caves
first learned to make fire and use it for all sorts of purposes.
In the future, the computational revolution is certain to be generally recognized as a transformation
as significant as, say, the Industrial Revolution.
The computer scientists in the study I referred to felt that, in the coming decades, lives
will be significantly enhanced by automated reasoning systems of different types. There
was considerable agreement that people will increasingly perceive these computer systems
systems as intelligent. Although many of these will be deployed behind the scenes, others
will be in the foreground, serving in an elegant, often collaborative manner to help people
do their jobs, to learn and teach, to reflect and remember, to plan and decide.
Without going into further detail about this at this point, let's turn to what prediction
psychologists had to make. Their key point was that psychological research would inevitably
become increasingly varied. It would move into such areas as behavioral economics and social
neuroscience. There is likely to be further expansion into domains with more practical
relevance as increasing numbers of women become research scientists, so areas such
as health, environment, family and social identity will receive more attention.
At the same time as they broaden their horizons, psychologists will also intensify their search
to discover what exactly determines how we act. They will be assisted in this by imaging
devices that will be inserted into the brain and provide a great deal of information
about how it behaves. There should be some fascinating discoveries coming to light very soon.
Another field that is currently undergoing enormous changes is that of genetics. It is
not new to suggest that average life expectancy is likely to continue rising in most countries.
However, today geneticists emphasize that it is vital that the increasing number of the elderly
in society must take quality of life into account. So how will genetics help this to happen?
To start with, they hope to develop technologies that can sequence each person's genome extremely
cheaply. This information about our DNA enables healthcare providers to predict our likelihood
of suffering from any particular disease.
From there on, it is a matter of weighing up various factors
with a view to determining what can be done to minimize
each individual's level of risk.
With such information in hand, new treatments will be developed
and the current one-size-fits-all approach to health care
will give way to a more personal approach.
The final subject area that I wish to bring to your attention is that of zoology. Once again,
computers and technology have a key role to play here. Experts comment specifically on the
importance of satellites for future developments in this field. These enable people to explore
the world from their homes, offices and schools. It is now possible, for instance,
to go online and see for yourself the abundant wildlife in one part of East Africa,
and in the surrounding region the harm people have done by destroying the forests,
all supposedly in the name of development.
Zoologists believe the breakthrough that lies ahead is how people act on such information as this.
They hope that we will learn to connect our minds to our hearts
and apply this knowledge to help protect our planet.
They express a clear hope that a greater understanding of the consequences of human short-sightedness
will make people anxious to rectify what we can before it is too late.
That is the end of Part 4. You now have one minute to check your answers to Part 4.
That is the end of the listening test.
You now have 10 minutes to transfer your answers to the listening answer sheet.

1.why: Mã đặt hàng là chuỗi số lẫn chữ: "The reference is 5174XCM".

2.why: Đi biển, trời ấm nên "the design you need is what we call our summer sleeping bag".

3.why: Dùng đệm hơi thay giường gấp; để bơm "You'll need a pump".

4.why: Nồi chảo mang từ nhà; "What we need to think about is water. We'll need a large bottle for that".

5.why: Cần đồ ăn không vỡ bằng kim loại: "So plates, then. A set of four in metal". Dao dĩa thì đã có.

6.why: Không muốn đèn pin nhựa vì bọn trẻ làm vỡ; "we've got some good rubber ones".

7.why: Đã có bóng; "do you have a baseball set? They'd love that".

8.why: "We need an up-to-date map of the area" – bản đồ cũ đã quá cũ.

9.why: Địa chỉ "56 Taupo Street", được đánh vần T-A-U-P-O.

10.why: Phí chuẩn $50, nhưng đơn trên $500 nên "a discounted delivery charge of only $25.50". Bẫy: 50 và 500.

11.why: Có 20 lối vào, "each connected to public roads by short paths" → B. Bẫy: xe buýt chỉ tới 2 điểm đầu cuối (C), bãi đỗ có camera chỉ ở 4 lối vào (A).

12.why: "In response to a poll of walkers last year, we've recently installed kiosks… with clear, easy-to-follow maps and other trail information" → C. Picnic và chỗ sạc đã có từ trước.

13.why: Red Rock Walk là cơ hội "to study a huge variety of vegetation" → A. Không nhìn được xa (B sai), chim thì "hard to spot" (C sai).

14.why: Mùa đông "if the weather conditions are really unsuitable, we might have to close this walk" → C. Sông vẫn đóng băng, tuyết dày (B sai) và thường đông người (A sai).

15.why: Giường tập thể: đặt trước không hiệu quả "so now we allocate them as people arrive" → H (ai đến trước được trước).

16.why: Phòng gia đình: "you will need to make arrangements ahead of time" → F (phải đặt trước).

17.why: "A popular facility that we've recently added is coin-operated washing machines" → G (thiết bị mới).

18.why: Bữa ăn có giá cố định, nhưng "We do ask you to give a hand with serving and cleaning up after meals" → D (nhờ khách giúp). Bẫy I: giá như nhau cho người lớn và trẻ em.

19.why: Tắm nước nóng "at no charge" → E (miễn phí).

20.why: "The hostel is in the process of creating a bike rental scheme which should be up and running next year" → C (chưa có).

21.why: Dầu gội từng là cách gội đầu tiết kiệm, nay "has evolved into a beauty product" → trở thành loại hàng hoá khác (C).

22.why: Nghiên cứu ở Yale cho thấy "bad hair days" "are not just imagined, and both sexes are equally affected" → chúng có thật (A). Nam nữ như nhau nên B sai.

23.why: Hầu hết nhà sản xuất dùng các hoá chất này "though they keep it quiet… strangely silent about it" → hiếm khi công khai (C).

24.why: In thẳng lên chai rẻ hơn 50% và nhanh hơn, nhưng "doesn't enhance the visual impact… comes across as a bit cheap" → trông kém hấp dẫn (B).

25.why: Bao bì thân thiện hơn "just by making it less heavy… I'd like to find out whether some of them actually do" → trọng lượng chai (B).

26.why: Michael ngại khuyến mãi, nhưng gặp nhãn mới "I'm usually up for giving it a go rather than sticking to one or two favourite brands" → C.

27.why: Quảng cáo Zing: gia đình hạnh phúc, nhà đẹp, người xem nghĩ "if only my life was like that" → lối sống đáng ghen tị (B).

28.why: Splash kể chuyện một cặp đôi chia tay hay ở lại với nhau → yếu tố tình cảm lãng mạn (F).

29.why: Just Go có nhiều thông tin kỹ thuật để khách tin rằng sản phẩm "will do the job they want it to" → độ tin cậy (E).

30.why: Brozene: không lời bình, "very calming with soft music and very peaceful imagery" → thư giãn (A).

31.why: Máy tính được ví như bước ngoặt khi tổ tiên trong hang "first learned to make fire". Lưu ý: đáp án trong key ghi "file", có thể là lỗi in của "fire".

32.why: "People will increasingly perceive these computer systems as intelligent".

33.why: Nghiên cứu tâm lý "would inevitably become increasingly varied".

34.why: "As increasing numbers of women become research scientists" – các lĩnh vực sức khoẻ, gia đình được chú ý hơn.

35.why: "Imaging devices that will be inserted into the brain".

36.why: Người già ngày càng nhiều nên phải tính tới "quality of life".

37.why: Giải mã gen giúp dự đoán "our likelihood of suffering from any particular disease".

38.why: Cách chữa "one-size-fits-all" sẽ nhường chỗ cho "a more personal approach".

39.why: Trên mạng thấy được tác hại "by destroying the forests".

40.why: "Apply this knowledge to help protect our planet".
